problem.text: The model comparison script hardcoded cuda:0 for both models' non-CPU modules.

reasoning.text: The change constructs one device from the command-line argument and uses it for both model branches, retaining the prefer_cpu override.

impact.text: Device selection becomes configurable without changing the sequential module-loading lifecycle or comparison formulas.

source_notes.text: The earlier deferred-loading entry was read. It establishes the module-scoped loading and handle-cleanup design and records an inherited perplexity indexing concern.

PR #26, “Superior 3INST parameters,” discusses using model_diff.py for decoder evaluation. Issue #33, “Error converting model,” initially reports file-opening failures and later uses the script to investigate GLM4 output. Their relationship to this change is inferred solely from the shared script; neither cited discussion establishes the motivation for device selection.

limitations: No Torch or CUDA execution was performed. Integer torch.device construction and its behavior across library versions and accelerator environments remain unverified.
Module.load and the base activation-transfer mechanism were inspected, but compatibility across every module override was not established.
The numerical check models only inherited perplexity slice bounds; it does not execute tensor operations or establish end-to-end metric correctness.

claims.text: The parser adds -d/--device as an integer with default 0 and help text “CUDA device index.” main immediately passes that integer to torch.device; it does not construct an explicit cuda:N string.

Both paired module loads receive the resulting device unless their prefer_cpu capability selects the unchanged 'cpu' branch. This is one shared device choice, not independent placement for A and B or multi-device sharding.

The base Module.load stores the supplied device and propagates it to submodules. prepare_for_device moves the activation to that stored device before forward. Consequently, changing the load destination also controls activation placement through the existing mechanism rather than a new explicit transfer in the script.

A still completes deferred loading, preparation, forward, unload, collection close and memory cleanup before B follows the same sequence. The new parser field supplies the attribute required by the new main entry statement; these edits work together.
Inspection of the parent together with the complete patch shows that the previously recorded perplexity axis-bound concern is carried over, not corrected by device selection.

findings.description: The unchanged nested perplexity helper bounds sequence slices using vocabulary size.
findings.trigger: The metrics loop receives more prediction positions than vocabulary entries, for example 2047 positions and vocabulary size 1024.
findings.actual_behavior: The loop stops at logits_.shape[1], covering only 1024 of those 2047 positions. Larger vocabularies can instead produce trailing empty slices.

verification.description: Whole-tree search located the helper's direct call in main's per-model metrics loop; other matches are the separately named test_ppl. The CLI invokes main, and the task patch leaves this helper and call unchanged.
verification.limits: Reach is established for the script's metrics loop, conditional on reaching it successfully.

verification.description: A standard-library model of the inspected loop covered 1024 of 2047 positions for vocabulary 1024; vocabulary 32000 covered all 2047 positions over four iterations.
verification.limits: This models integer bounds, not repository execution or Torch empty-slice behavior.

annotation.summary: Adds a shared device-index option to model_diff.py while preserving CPU-preferred modules, sequential loading and existing metrics.
